old_caption:
The video begins with a close-up shot of a white piece of paper placed on a dark surface. The paper contains handwritten text and diagrams. At the top left corner, the letters "CD" are written in purple marker. Below this, there is a horizontal line followed by the word "LABEL" written in orange marker. Underneath "LABEL," the word "LACQUER" is written in black marker. Further down, the word "PLASTIC" is written in green marker. To the right of these labels, there is one set of measurements: "METAL 50-100 nm," written in green marker.

Below the labels and measurements, there is a single wavy line drawn in black marker, resembling a cross-section or diagram of a layered structure. The labels "LACQUER" and "PLASTIC" are positioned above the line, corresponding to their respective layers. The camera remains mostly static, then moves slightly to the left, revealing a CD next to the paper, with light reflecting off its surface.
original_wisa_caption:
The video begins with a close-up shot of a white piece of paper placed on a dark surface. The paper contains handwritten text and diagrams. At the top left corner, the letters "EB" are written in purple marker. Below this, there is a horizontal line followed by the word "LABEL" written in orange marker. Underneath "LABEL," the word "LACQUER" is written in black marker. Further down, the word "PLASTIC" is written in green marker. To the right of these labels, there are two sets of measurements: "METAL 50-100 nm" and "PLASTIC 50-100 nm," both written in green marker.

Below the labels and measurements, there are several rectangular shapes drawn in black marker, resembling a cross-section or diagram of a layered structure. These rectangles are labeled with "LACQUER" and "PLASTIC" at the bottom, corresponding to their respective layers.
caption: A white hand-drawn card rests on a dark textured surface, showing a labeled cross-section diagram of a compact disc. The purple heading reads CD above black boundary lines, while orange LABEL and LACQUER sit over a gray METAL 50-100nm note. A stepped, foil-like strip catches the light between the metal line and the green PLASTIC label, and red LASER text with two upward arrows points from below. Through much of the clip the card stays nearly centered. Only small perspective and lighting shifts occur, and the drawn strip keeps reflecting bright spots. Later the view blurs as the card drifts toward the right edge, and a real rainbow-colored disc appears on the left. The actual CD shows its central hole and a bright white reflection on its upper surface. A blue-purple glowing spot sits near its rim, while a hand enters from the right beside the card.

Write a corrected WISA-style training caption for this exact video clip.
This clip is a temporally cropped excerpt, with arbitrary start and end boundaries. It is NOT
necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
